To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The stimulation site in TMS can be determined from the induced electric field distribution in the brain.

(a) the stimulation site on the cortical surface is located in the lateral part of hand knob in the central sulcus, (b) it is smaller than the electric field induced in the cortex, and (c) it can be determined with the presented method. [1]

the electric field induced at the cortex by a TMS coil is larger than the cortical region stimulated by the induced current and the most likely stimulation region on the cortex is located in the lateral part of motor cortex.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between the physical stimulation parameters and the physiological response in TMS.
the development and testing of a new method to determine the stimulation site in TMS.
the development of a method to determine the cortical stimulation site and its size in TMS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electric field distribution is a necessary but not sufficient condition for the stimulation of cortical tissue.
the motor threshold is the intensity of the magnetic field at the cortex that produces a certain amount of current flow in the cortex.
the electric field induced at the head by a TMS coil is only one of the parameters that determine the stimulated area on the cortex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a method to link the physics of TMS with the physiology of the brain.
the motor cortex is stimulated by a sphere field with a radius of 2.5 +/- 1.0 mm.
the motor cortex is a very small target area for TMS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stimulation site is located at the lateral edge of the central sulcus.

the stimulation site is not the same as the center of gravity of the coil position distribution and that motor thresholds are not a measure of cortical excitability but of the electric field strength.

TMS can only stimulate a limited region of the cortex, even when the coil is positioned over the center of the motor cortex, and that this region is much smaller than the size and shape of the induced electric field.
